learning: Iteration 1 showed line losses falling from 1-2 to 1 per run while all runs still left the track at 11-16% progress, so the span and lead are the limits. Check line_loss_events, max_error and progress on all three development tracks. If the signal saturates or line losses remain, the span or gains need changing.
notes: Complete package for the Builder's seven-sensor ±6 cm array at a 3 cm lead, with weights scaled to x/0.03 so the slope matches iteration 1. kd rises to 0.15 for the closer lead, and wheel_track drops to 0.10 m. Full measurement set requested.
rationale: The only race evidence is iteration 0 (entityR2B, 60 trials, no finishes) and iteration 1 (entityR2B, 60 trials, no finishes). Iteration 1 cut line losses from 1-2 to 1 per run, but every run still went off track at 11-16% progress with max_error of 0.061-0.066 m. The sensor span and lead are the main limits, not the gains. The Builder's proposal widens the array to 7 sensors spanning ±6 cm at 2 cm pitch, with 16 mm footprints so neighbouring sensors overlap the 25 mm tape. Sensor weights are x/0.03, giving [-2, -1.333, -0.667, 0, 0.667, 1.333, 2]. This keeps the same signal slope as iteration 1 (±2 at 3 cm offset), so the gains kp 3.0 and kd 0.1 carry over without rescaling. The left-positive ordering matches the convention, so a positive weight on the left sensor steers left. The lead moves to 3 cm, which reads bends earlier. A closer lead gives less time to react, so I raise kd slightly to 0.15 to damp the faster response. The wheel track drops to 0.10 m to turn more readily, and mass stays at 0.6 kg. base_speed stays at 1.6 and ki at 0, since progress has not yet been limited by speed or integral action. line_loss stays 'last_direction' because the tape still leaves the array on the sharpest bends. Expected result, not measured: line_loss_events near 0, max_error below 0.06 m, and progress well above 0.15. If the robot still leaves the track with few line losses, the lead or gains are the limit.
